raw_text: The conflict terrain coordinate got the same treatment as the social-field quadrant. The model now returns a continuous terrain distance, and the terrain category is derived from it by bin edges instead of being trusted as a drawn label. A live call confirmed the model does return the position, so the derivation is really in force and not silently falling back. On that draw the Cotton case sat mid-range in "drifting," not on a boundary. Whether the distance moves between sittings is now an open question. The gain is in how instability appears: a flip that used to look like an unexplained category change now shows up as a number moving, which can be reasoned about. One decision remains open. The terrain bin edges (thirds) don't match the tension band thresholds used by cross-scale (0.4 and 0.7). Aligning them costs nothing now, but once a post-fix baseline exists it would mean throwing that baseline away.
